stem: Mice are fed a harmless protein together with cholera toxin as adjuvant. Several days later, secretory IgA against the protein is found in their intestinal secretions.
oneliner: Mice fed protein + cholera toxin adjuvant → secretory IgA in gut secretions → where is the antigen first sampled?
ask: At which site does the gut IgA response to the fed antigen begin?

options.A: Subcapsular sinus of a mesenteric lymph node
options.B: M cells in the epithelium over Peyer patches

whyNot.A: Lymph nodes receive **antigen already carried from the gut**, after sampling at the epithelium
whyNot.C: The spleen handles **blood-borne** antigen, not a fed one
whyNot.D: Site of **T-cell negative selection**, not response to ingested antigen
whyNot.E: Home to **long-lived plasma cells**, not the first antigen contact

answer: M cells over Peyer patches (gut-associated lymphoid tissue)
why: **M cells** in the follicle-associated epithelium take up luminal antigen and pass it to **Peyer patch** dendritic cells and B cells. **TGF-β** and Th cell help drive **class switching to IgA**. IgA plasma cells then secrete **dimeric IgA**, which crosses the epithelium as **secretory IgA**.

idea.rule: Mucosal IgA begins with M cells passing luminal antigen to Peyer patch lymphoid follicles.
also: Dimeric IgA is joined by a J chain and carried across epithelium by the poly-Ig receptor
Secretory component protects IgA from digestion
Oral polio vaccine induces gut IgA
Oral cholera and rotavirus vaccines also work through gut IgA
